de_identification: Emails removed, timestamps removed, row order shuffled
key_facts: n = 1,478 total responses summarized in the published tables
18 world regions with no country-level data
MCP tools focus on published summary tables and crosstabs, while REST downloads also expose de-identified row-level responses
headlines: The most-used design tool after Figma is now an AI: Claude at 50.8% weekly usage
Top weekly tools: Figma (82.6%), Claude (50.8%), ChatGPT (48.2%)
43.8% of designers spend 50%+ of their building time on AI-generated code (vibe coding)
The profession split into thirds: 37.7% zero, 18.5% some, 43.8% majority AI-generated
Design engineers: 80.9% vibe code 50%+ while IC designers are at 35.0%
59.1% have built their own tool with AI in the last 6 months
Satisfaction rises from 5.93/10 among zero-vibe respondents to 7.39/10 among heavy vibe coders
Design engineers: 50.0% feel more valuable, 10.6% less secure. Researchers: 17.4% more valuable, 39.1% less secure
data_caveats: Public APIs expose both published summary tables and row-level respondent data
Researcher (n=23) should be treated as directional only
One malformed role value in the raw CSV is excluded from role-based aggregate tables
Multi-select questions sum to more than 100%
Cross-tab percentages are calculated within each role's n
endpoints: GET /responses — de-identified respondent rows as JSON
GET /download/responses-json — de-identified respondent rows as JSON download
GET /download/responses-csv — de-identified respondent rows as CSV download
POST /agent/query — natural language (API key may be required for non-first-party access)
